changes: Add four explicit uninitialized constructors returning Array1/Array2 of MaybeUninit<T>, with no Default or Clone requirement on T.

Add consuming unsafe assume_init transitions for Copy elements. Transfer an owned Vec with identical pointer, length and capacity using into_raw_parts/from_raw_parts. Borrowed and shared slices keep their original lifetime and provenance; no initialization transition allocates or invokes element construction/copy callbacks.

Require valid initialized T in every actual flat slot before transition, including slots outside matrix metadata after inherited backing replacement or resize. Spare owned capacity and unborrowed external tails are not accessible elements and need not be initialized.
Keep ordinary initialized constructors and all original assertions unchanged. No shared allocator or allocation routing changes are made.
probe_policy: The native payload is statically asserted trivially default constructible/copyable. Fifteen rows cover linear size/bounds, matrix size/bounds, empty ranges, negative origins, mutable borrowed prefixes, and actual matrix flat backing resized to zero/shorter/longer lengths. Every slot is assigned before any native read. Seven Rust tests compare all rows; five Rust-only tests cover safe invalid-dimension guards, borrowed reference lifetimes, shared read-only detachment and zero-sized elements. One library unit test transfers an initialized length with spare uninitialized Vec capacity and verifies identical pointer/length/capacity.

initial_failure.cause: The crate denies unsafe_code by default. The first build omitted existing-style localized allow attributes for the new audited unsafe transition/helper operations. The functions now carry focused allows with explicit safety contracts; no Miri validation or provenance flags were relaxed.

limitations: These constructors explicitly select the uninitialized storage policy; Rust traits do not infer the native C++ is_trivially_default_constructible predicate. Existing Default constructors still select initialized Rust storage.

The unsafe initialization transition is a Rust representation adapter, not another native declaration. It requires Copy so shared-view detachment remains expressible without constructing a new cloning contract for arbitrary T. Its two compiler bodies earn no additional native mapping credit.
No native uninitialized value is read or compared. Native invalid/uninitialized reads, object-lifetime violations and signed bounds arithmetic overflow remain outside the claim.

All actual inherited backing slots must be initialized, even if shorter/longer than rectangular metadata. Native changed-base cases use Array1::Resize while Rust reconstructs the same backing state; this does not claim a new uninitialized Resize entry point.

The initialization transition does not allocate, move elements or clone them. Vec owner identity, allocation pointer, length and capacity transfer intact; borrowed/shared lifetimes remain unchanged. Current arrays use their existing Vec allocation and gain no native allocator-routing claim.
Shared read-only storage retains the Rust detachment policy after later mutable access. This transition does not close the native writable const-cast alias domain.
Arbitrary raw overlapping wrappers, multiple internal Emplace arguments, nontrivial constructor failure leaks, throwing destructors and native allocator hooks remain open.
The protected native trivial construct branches explain the constructor policy but are not separately exposed as raw pointer callbacks. The class checklist retains those unresolved protocol domains.
All four constructor bindings remain partial; global API inventory and original legacy mapping credit are unchanged.
